title: Slow down in built-up areas
body: Urban roads in Lagos, Abuja, and Kano often have pedestrians, okadas, and potholes. Stay at or below 50 km/h in towns unless signs say otherwise. Speed limits save lives when traffic is unpredictable.

title: Buckle up every trip
body: FRSC requires front-seat belts and recommends rear belts too. Check that passengers are secured before moving, especially children. A short trip without a belt is still risky on Nigerian roads.

title: Drive with care at night
body: Many roads lack street lighting. Use low beams in traffic, high beams only when alone, and reduce speed. Watch for broken-down vehicles, animals, and unmarked speed bumps.

title: Rain and wet-season driving
body: During heavy rain, increase following distance and avoid sudden braking. Harmattan dust reduces visibility—use wipers and headlights. If water covers the road, do not guess the depth; turn back if unsure.

title: Approach junctions slowly
body: At T-junctions and roundabouts, assume others may not yield. Look left-right-left, signal early, and avoid blocking the intersection. Motorcycles often filter—check mirrors before turning.
